prompts.text:
Walking into a whole different dimension.

Prompt: 
Use my uploaded portrait/selfie as the ONLY identity and facial reference. Preserve my recognizable facial identity and appearance naturally.

Vertical streetwear campaign poster: a woman with the face from the reference photo stands frontally at the center of an arid dusk plain, arms hanging at her sides, shoulders relaxed, looking straight into the lens with a completely neutral catalogue expression, no gesture. Around her, articulated zebra skeletons stand scattered across the plain in near-perfect symmetry — two large ones cropped by the left and right frame edges, two mid-sized further in, one small at center right — the fan arrangement building depth through decreasing scale. Wardrobe (womenswear): an oversized camel-beige hooded sweatshirt with a central block graphic print — an ornate cross motif with layered text and photographic portrait panels in red and blue; extremely wide-leg military camouflage cargo trousers in green and brown with bellowed side pockets, vertical zips and webbing straps hanging from the waist; and dark chunky-soled boots. Lighting, deliberately inconsistent between layers: the subject lit with soft even frontal studio light, broad fill, no hard shadows, flat descriptive modelling on the face; the environment lit by a low side source throwing long skeleton shadows to the right, plus a blue backlight at the horizon igniting the mist. She casts her own shorter, softer shadow to the right to bed her in. Atmosphere: volumetric blue haze spread at mid height across the whole scene, denser toward the sides and the back — separating the planes, washing out the horizon and fusing the edges of the composited figure into the environment. Post texture: an overlay of analogue degradation across the entire image — fine vertical scratch lines, dust specks, coarse grain and a slight overall softness, equalising the texture between the studio subject and the background. Grade: a very strong blue-cyan cast through the whole frame, lifted blacks with a cool tint, low saturation everywhere except the hoodie print; the only warmth is the camel sweatshirt and the skin tones, deliberately protected from the cast so the subject separates from the cold surroundings. Camera: vertical framing at chest height, frontal and centered, medium-long focal length with no distortion, deep depth of field with atmospheric rather than optical falloff. Typographic layer: three lines of scattered alphanumeric characters interspersed with pedestrian pictograms across the top, in wide-tracked white condensed sans-serif — signage or inventory-code language; at the bottom center, a brand name in a narrow serif with a small sans-serif line beneath it. Palette: blue-cyan dominating absolutely across sky, mist and ground; camel-beige hoodie as the single warm block and exact center of attention; camo green and brown as the earthy bridge downward; white bone scattered in a ring around; and the print’s red as the only saturated accent in the frame.

prompts.text:
Tied up in the drama, but the outfit stays clean.

Prompt: 
A conceptual marionette composite: two giant hands enter the frame from the upper left and upper right corners, fingers draped with white puppet strings that descend in an inverted triangle to a woman with the face from the reference photo standing at normal scale against a concrete block wall, the strings tied around her wrists and one knee. Her body language is pure puppet — arms hanging with limp broken wrists, one leg bent inward and lifted, torso slumped back against the wall as if held up only by the strings — mouth slightly open, looking straight into the lens. The strings and the giant hands cast no shadow on the wall while the woman casts a hard defined one, a deliberate inconsistency that keeps the hands reading as a separate plane of reality rather than part of the scene.

Wardrobe on the woman: a green full-zip racing track jacket with a stand collar, white piping along the shoulders and sleeves, elasticated hem and cuffs, a white “HOPEFULLY” script across the chest, a small checkered-flag shield patch, “A WINNER NEVER QUITS” printed at the left chest and sponsor-style lettering down both sleeves; a black high-neck top underneath; layered silver ball-chain necklaces with a cross pendant; a black flat-brim snapback cap with small white embroidery and a silver dollar-sign logo on the side; black wraparound sunglasses with dark opaque lenses; extremely wide-leg black cargo trousers with silver rivet studs down the legs and a long studded black leather belt hanging loose from the waistband; and chunky white platform sneakers. The giant hands are loaded with gold — wide signet rings, a gold-dial watch worn as a ring, a white-and-gold wristwatch, and stacked rigid gold bangles and bracelets on both wrists — the gold being the only strongly specular material in the frame.

Environment: a grey concrete block wall in running bond with deep raked joints forming a regular grid that orders the tangle of strings, a galvanized steel post bolted to the wall on the left, a barred window at the upper right, a darker block plinth and cement pavement below, and a wedge of blue sky in the upper left corner. Lighting: hard direct mid-afternoon sun from the front-left — a short crisp shadow thrown by the woman onto the blocks at her right, sharp shadows from the post and window bars, strong modelling across the knuckles of both giant hands, a hard glint sliding across the dark sunglass lenses; high contrast, highlights near clipping on the gold and the silver studs, deep but open shadows lifted by bounce off the pale concrete. Camera: vertical framing at chest height, square to the wall, symmetrical theatrical composition with the two hands as parentheses in the upper corners and the woman at the lower vertex, deep depth of field with only slight softness on the near hands. Palette: concrete grey dominating almost entirely as the neutral ground, racing green as the single saturated accent holding the exact center against black trousers, white piping and platform sneakers as the light values, gold jewelry as the metallic accent repeating at both top corners, and the sliver of blue sky as the only other cool note.

#webtomind #AI写真 #攻壳机动队风义体特工

本期把「攻壳机动队风格」编译成一组四张的画面合同，叙事按建立、变化、转折、余韵推进：

义体锚点：金属关节线与光学迷彩外层微光，是识别角色、不靠标题解释世界观的唯一符号；

场景叙事：检修舱、积水窄巷、高楼速降、全息广告街口——每张都先回答"她为什么在这里、正在做什么"；

镜头语言：50mm 检修近景 → 28mm 积水低机位 → 楼顶极限俯拍速降 → 85mm 全息街口半身，四张机位、景别、光色全部错开；

表情绑定：表情与动作、视线、落点同向——检修中的专注、雨停间隙的警觉松弛、速降中的冷静、仰望全息屏的审视。

每张只保留一个动作、一个视觉焦点、一套单主光。以速降一张为例，完整提示词如下。

【GPT Image2提示词】

主题：高楼滑绳速降义体特工写真（攻壳机动队风格致敬，原创角色）

主体：成年女性义体特工全身入镜，面部身份与身体比例由唯一参考图锁定

人物·表情：眼神专注看向下方速降落点，嘴唇微抿，表情是任务执行中的冷静专注，动作熟练没有犹豫；视线与身体朝向一致，前因是楼顶速降点，后果是她正落向的下一层平台

服装·姿势：低弧深 V 领口的深紫黑压缩战术内搭配完整不透明内层，外搭半透明光学迷彩短外套（边缘热扩散微光），高腰压缩长裤，金属义体臂带关节缝线，沿速降绳滑降的中段，一只手握速降制动器，另一只手轻扶墙面或速降腰带，一脚蹬墙、另一腿微屈保持平衡

背景·光线：高楼玻璃幕墙外墙，城市霓虹灯海为背景光，楼顶侧逆光为唯一主光，轮廓光只落发丝、肩线与衣摆边缘，玻璃幕墙反射连续不碎

构图·镜头：从楼顶边缘偏侧的极限俯拍，速降绳与人物形成清楚垂直线，人物占据画面中央，下方城市方格灯光与玻璃幕墙反光为纵深

质感·风格：机能面料与霓虹冷色混合，光学迷彩边缘微光克制，金属义体与速降扣具窄高光，皮肤保留自然纹理，轻微电影颗粒

负面：不出现官方名称、Logo、真实品牌字、第二动作、复杂手势、肢体夸张变形、绳索缠绕身体、霓虹光斑落脸、脸部光斑

Prompt:

Create an ultra-premium Instagram social media campaign poster for Maersk that looks like an official global brand campaign designed by Pentagram, AKQA, or DesignStudio for Behance and Cannes Lions.

Aspect ratio 4:5 vertical, 8K ultra-high resolution, hyper-realistic commercial advertising, premium editorial composition, Scandinavian minimalist design language, bold corporate branding, clean visual hierarchy, generous negative space.

Scene: A massive modern Maersk logistics hub at sunrise. In the foreground, a pristine Maersk-blue electric container truck drives confidently toward the camera from a premium logistics terminal. The truck is loaded with an official Maersk shipping container featuring the authentic Maersk star logo and corporate blue livery. The vehicle is positioned in a dramatic front three-quarter perspective, becoming the visual hero of the composition.

Behind it, a state-of-the-art container terminal is alive with activity. Giant ship-to-shore cranes lift containers with precision, automated guided vehicles move seamlessly through the yard, and neatly stacked Maersk containers create a strong geometric rhythm. In the distance, an enormous Maersk container vessel is docked at the terminal with hundreds of containers onboard. Above the horizon, a modern cargo aircraft climbs into the sky, completing the end-to-end logistics story from sea to air.

Human presence adds life to the campaign: logistics managers in safety helmets reviewing operations on digital tablets, crane operators coordinating container movement, forklift operators transporting cargo, dock workers inspecting containers, all captured naturally without looking at the camera. Every action feels authentic, creating a living industrial ecosystem rather than a staged corporate photo.

The environment is clean, engineered and premium, inspired by Scandinavian industrial architecture with polished concrete, glass control towers, organized container stacks, calm ocean water, crisp blue skies and subtle atmospheric haze. The entire logistics hub feels efficient, sustainable and technologically advanced.

The composition is bold and highly graphic. Oversized white negative space balances the industrial scene. Massive editorial typography reading “MOVE THE WORLD.” integrates into the architecture, partially overlapping containers without hiding important subjects. Thin technical grid lines, subtle route graphics, coordinate markers and minimal logistics-inspired design elements reinforce Maersk's engineering precision. Large Maersk-blue geometric panels anchor the composition, creating a modern corporate visual system without clutter.

Colour palette: authentic Maersk Blue (#42B0D5), pure white, soft concrete grey, steel grey, deep ocean blue with restrained safety yellow accents. Scandinavian minimalism, clean contrast, premium corporate aesthetic.

Lighting: bright natural morning daylight, soft diffused sunlight, realistic reflections on painted metal, shipping containers, truck bodywork and glass architecture, crisp atmospheric depth, premium commercial automotive and industrial photography.

Captured on a Phase One XF IQ4 150MP medium-format camera with a Schneider Kreuznach 55mm lens, ultra-high dynamic range, razor-sharp details, realistic container textures, steel surfaces, tyre rubber, glass reflections, painted metal, subtle wear, authentic industrial materials, natural human skin texture and premium color science.

The final image should feel like the hero cover of a Behance case study for Maersk's global integrated logistics campaign—modern, bold, clean, highly designed, unmistakably premium, and instantly recognizable as an official Maersk social media advertisement.

prompts.text:
First things first -> GPT 2.5 Flare prompt for the ref still

DIRECTIVE:
Produce one still that reads as an unpublished photograph taken by a working photographer. Optical capture, available physics, lived-in detail.

SUBJECT:
A three-seat floral couch, faded brown and orange 1980s upholstery with sagging cushions, floating about four meters above a trailer park lot under a huge tight cluster of roughly fifty large white weather balloons tied to its frame with mismatched cords. Three Arizona trailer park neighbors sit on it side by side, men in their forties and fifties: a heavy sunburnt man with a grey moustache, a wiry tanned man with a long goatee, a broad Mexican-American man with tattooed forearms.
Sun-bleached trucker caps, stretched tank tops and a faded gas station T-shirt, cargo shorts, cheap rubber flip-flops dangling from bare feet in the air. Each one holds a dented beer can.
Flat, dead serious faces, slouched like men on a porch, each minding his own thing: one squints toward the low sun, one looks down his fishing line, one stares into his can.

ACTION / BEAT:
The couch hangs tilted a few degrees, tugging upward against a green garden hose stretched tight as a guitar string from the couch leg down to the trailer hitch ball of a rusty pickup. The hasty hose loop is halfway off the chrome ball, one more inch from sliding free. The wiry man fishes straight down with a rod, his line dropping toward an inflatable kiddie pool and passing close to a clothesline full of laundry. The broad man rests a wooden slingshot on his knees. A red cooler dangles under the couch on a rope like an anchor, a small portable grill is zip-tied to the armrest with a thin thread of smoke, and an aluminum ladder stands below, its top rung a full meter short of the couch. A scruffy tan mutt sits by the pickup bumper staring at the slipping hose loop.
A caught moment.

SCENE:
A worn trailer park on the edge of the Arizona desert, single-wide trailers with sun-chalked aluminum siding.
Late afternoon, dry heat, cloudless pale sky, sun low and hard.
A 1990s pickup with oxidized paint and a cracked tail light, a half-deflated blue kiddie pool with a yellow duck float, a sagging clothesline with towels and a floral housedress, cracked asphalt patched with tar and oil stains, a dented trash barrel, dry weeds along a leaning chain-link fence, a saguaro and power lines far behind.
A room or street that has already been used.

COMPOSITION:
Shot type: long zoom, full view of the floating couch, the balloon cluster and the pickup below it
Angle: slight low, from the window of the trailer next door
Placement: off-center, couch and balloons in the upper left, pickup and dog in the lower right, the green hose cutting a diagonal between them, horizon tilted
Look-room: right
Foreground: mild occlusion, a dusty aluminum window frame and a torn corner of insect screen blurring the left edge and the bottom of the frame
Crop: handheld, slightly imperfect, the top balloons clipped by the frame edge.

CAMERA PACK:
Body: Google Pixel 9 Pro
Lens / zoom: 5x telephoto pushed to Super Res Zoom around 8x
Aperture or phone mode: default auto mode, shot in a hurry through the window
Focus: sharp on the couch and the three men, natural falloff behind, the window frame soft and close
Film or sensor: computational RAW with zoom mush, oversharpened edges on the balloons and a little heat haze over the asphalt

LIGHT:
Source: low desert sun from the right side
Quality: hard sun, raking and unflattering, long shadows
Color temperature: warm late-afternoon daylight against a pale blue sky
Shadows follow that source.

PHOTOGRAPHIC CHARACTER:
Visible skin microtexture, pores, sunburn, faint uneven tone, slight facial asymmetry.
Flyaway hairs. Fabric weave, seams, pills, dust, scuffs on the couch upholstery and the caps.
Matte latex balloons with dusty, uneven surfaces and creases at the necks; kinked, sun-faded rubber on the hose; pitted chrome on the hitch ball.
Grain or sensor texture that matches the camera pack.
Catchlights only from the stated light.
Highlights a little hot, shadows a little closed.
Candid stance, catalog-unaware.

Animate it with Seedance 2.5 and this prompt:

RAW HOME PHONE VIDEO.

One single continuous 30-second recording with no cuts at all, made on a smartphone by a neighbor standing inside his trailer, holding the phone up to the open window, uploaded unedited.

The phone never stops recording and never jumps: every change of view comes from the neighbor moving the phone, zooming or tilting.

The window frame and a torn bug screen edge show at the left and bottom of the picture now and then as he moves.

Amateur handheld, natural shake, clumsy jerky pinch-zooms in and out, autofocus that hunts when things move, auto exposure that blows out the bright desert sky, ordinary phone noise, true-to-life colors.

No overlays, no text on screen, no music.

The neighbor is never still and nothing in the picture is ever still.

[ref_still]

locks the people and the place:

- The same three guys:
  - One in a white tank top and trucker cap.
  - One in a gray tank top and cap.
  - One in a dark t-shirt and cap.
  - All in shorts and flip-flops.

- The same worn floral orange sofa with the big cluster of white balloons tied to it with ropes.
- The small black kettle grill strapped to one armrest.
- The red cooler hanging from the sofa.
- The long green rope tied to the hitch ball of the old pickup.
- The dirt yard.
- The clothesline with laundry.
- The inflatable pool with the yellow duck.
- The aluminum ladder.
- The white trailer homes.
- The saguaro.
- The power lines.
- The scruffy tan dog.

Warm late-afternoon desert light.

OPENING — 0:00

The recording opens on the whole scene seen from the window.

The sofa sits on the dirt, straining upward on its ropes, the balloons bobbing and bumping into each other above it.

Two of the guys are on the ladder and on the ground tying the last ropes to the sofa legs.

The third pulls a knot tight with his teeth.

The dog trots back and forth around them, sniffing and wagging.

LIFT-OFF — ~0:02

After about two seconds they finish and step back.

The sofa lifts a few centimeters off the dirt and the three guys scramble and jump onto it one after another, landing on the cushions.

With their weight it drops back down, scrapes the ground and wobbles, then starts climbing again.

The neighbor pinch-zooms in clumsily and back out while the dog runs in a circle and jumps toward the sofa.

ASCENDING

Without any break, the sofa keeps climbing slowly with the green rope unrolling from the pickup hitch.

The guys celebrate:

- High-fives.
- Fists in the air.
- One cracks a beer from the cooler and drinks.
- Another lifts the lid of the grill, smoke puffing out, grabs a burger with tongs and hands it to his buddy, who takes a big bite.
- They laugh, point at the houses below and rock the sofa.

The neighbor zooms in on them, loses focus, and zooms back out to show the rope getting tight.

ROPE TENSION

The green rope pulls tight from the hitch ball with a jolt and the sofa stops a few meters up, swaying and slowly turning on the end of the rope.

The guys bounce with the jolt, then settle in:

- Chatting.
- One stretches his arms behind his head.
- One passes beers around.
- One flips another burger.
- They wave down at the yard.

Below, the dog backs away a few steps from the rope and barks up at them nonstop.

THE CAT

Still in the same continuous recording, a black cat walks in from the left across the dirt with its tail straight up, calm, ignoring the barking dog.

It hops onto the pickup's bumper, sits next to the hitch ball and stares at the knot of the green rope.

The neighbor pinch-zooms in on the cat, shaky and half out of focus, whispering:

"no, no, no"

Above, the guys keep drinking and laughing without noticing.

THE SNAP

The cat swipes once at the rope with its claws and the green rope snaps free from the hitch.

The sofa shoots up into the sky, the loose rope whipping behind it.

The guys grab the armrests and each other, screaming in panic.

A beer can and a burger fall off.

FINAL MOMENT

The neighbor zooms out fast and tilts the phone up to follow the sofa as it gets smaller and smaller against the blue sky, the screams fading.

Below, the cat licks its paw by the hitch and the dog runs in circles barking at the sky.

The recording keeps following the sofa until the last instant.

SOUND

Sound throughout: only what the phone picks up through the window.

- Balloons squeaking.
- Rope creaking.
- The dog panting and barking.
- The guys laughing, whooping, chatting and finally screaming.
- A can opening.
- The grill lid clanking.
- Wind.
- The neighbor's breathing.
- His disbelieving laugh at the end.

No music.

Enjoy! 🫡

No overlays, no text on screen, no music.

The neighbor is never still and nothing in the picture is ever still.

locks the people and the place:

- The same three guys:
  - One in a white tank top and trucker cap.
  - One in a gray tank top and cap.
  - One in a dark t-shirt and cap.
  - All in shorts and flip-flops.

- The same worn floral orange sofa with the big cluster of white balloons tied to it with ropes.
- The small black kettle grill strapped to one armrest.
- The red cooler hanging from the sofa.
- The long green rope tied to the hitch ball of the old pickup.
- The dirt yard.
- The clothesline with laundry.
- The inflatable pool with the yellow duck.
- The aluminum ladder.
- The white trailer homes.
- The saguaro.
- The power lines.
- The scruffy tan dog.

Warm late-afternoon desert light.

OPENING — 0:00

The recording opens on the whole scene seen from the window.

The sofa sits on the dirt, straining upward on its ropes, the balloons bobbing and bumping into each other above it.

Two of the guys are on the ladder and on the ground tying the last ropes to the sofa legs.

The third pulls a knot tight with his teeth.

The dog trots back and forth around them, sniffing and wagging.

LIFT-OFF — ~0:02

After about two seconds they finish and step back.

The sofa lifts a few centimeters off the dirt and the three guys scramble and jump onto it one after another, landing on the cushions.

With their weight it drops back down, scrapes the ground and wobbles, then starts climbing again.

The neighbor pinch-zooms in clumsily and back out while the dog runs in a circle and jumps toward the sofa.

ASCENDING

Without any break, the sofa keeps climbing slowly with the green rope unrolling from the pickup hitch.

The guys celebrate:

- High-fives.
- Fists in the air.
- One cracks a beer from the cooler and drinks.
- Another lifts the lid of the grill, smoke puffing out, grabs a burger with tongs and hands it to his buddy, who takes a big bite.
- They laugh, point at the houses below and rock the sofa.

The neighbor zooms in on them, loses focus, and zooms back out to show the rope getting tight.

ROPE TENSION

The green rope pulls tight from the hitch ball with a jolt and the sofa stops a few meters up, swaying and slowly turning on the end of the rope.

The guys bounce with the jolt, then settle in:

- Chatting.
- One stretches his arms behind his head.
- One passes beers around.
- One flips another burger.
- They wave down at the yard.

Below, the dog backs away a few steps from the rope and barks up at them nonstop.

THE CAT

Still in the same continuous recording, a black cat walks in from the left across the dirt with its tail straight up, calm, ignoring the barking dog.

It hops onto the pickup's bumper, sits next to the hitch ball and stares at the knot of the green rope.

The neighbor pinch-zooms in on the cat, shaky and half out of focus, whispering:

"no, no, no"

Above, the guys keep drinking and laughing without noticing.

THE SNAP

The cat swipes once at the rope with its claws and the green rope snaps free from the hitch.

The sofa shoots up into the sky, the loose rope whipping behind it.

The guys grab the armrests and each other, screaming in panic.

A beer can and a burger fall off.

FINAL MOMENT

The neighbor zooms out fast and tilts the phone up to follow the sofa as it gets smaller and smaller against the blue sky, the screams fading.

Below, the cat licks its paw by the hitch and the dog runs in circles barking at the sky.

The recording keeps following the sofa until the last instant.

SOUND

Sound throughout: only what the phone picks up through the window.

- Balloons squeaking.
- Rope creaking.
- The dog panting and barking.
- The guys laughing, whooping, chatting and finally screaming.
- A can opening.
- The grill lid clanking.
- Wind.
- The neighbor's breathing.
- His disbelieving laugh at the end.

No music.

Enjoy! 🫡

INPUT_TOPIC ::= "<insert city / neighborhood / district>"  [TOPIC_ANALYSIS] From INPUT_TOPIC, infer and assign: - STRUCTURE: the single most iconic mixed-use building of that place (tenement, machiya, brownstone, kiosk-tower, shophouse), 4–6 stories. - STRATA: 4–5 vertically stacked zones, bottom to top — cellar/utility, ground-floor commerce, mid residential, upper residential, roof world — each with its own function and palette. - RESIDENTS: 6–8 locals distributed across strata, each mid-action and true to that floor (shopkeeper, cook, repair worker, kid, elder, cat). - STREET_LIFE: 2–3 figures and a vehicle on the sliver of pavement at the base. - EASTER_EGGS: 12+ local props, signage in the right script, and one DEEP_CUT native detail tucked in a corner. - LIGHT_LOGIC: cellar bare-bulb, shop neon/awning shade, warm apartment lamps, blue TV glow, open-sky roof.  <scene> ::= <shell> + <strata_grid> + <residents> + <dense_dressing> + <render_env> <shell> ::= "a single isometric building-block of STRUCTURE with two adjoining façades and the roof cut away on a clean vertical section line, a thin strip of its own street at the base, floating in a plain neutral void, true architecture, real local materials and weathering" <strata_grid> ::= "STRATA stacked floor over floor inside the shell — each a fully realized tiny room with its own [LIGHT_LOGIC], flooring, furniture and a connecting stair or ladder, separated by visible slab floors and party walls" <residents> ::= "RESIDENTS placed one-to-two per floor, each genuinely doing something tied to that level, correctly scaled to the furniture; two of them interacting across a stairwell or window; STREET_LIFE below" <dense_dressing> ::= "EASTER_EGGS distributed by floor — goods, posters, laundry, pipes, clutter that is full but readable — with the DEEP_CUT tucked into one corner" <render_env> ::= "clean 3D render, soft global illumination plus the per-floor practical lights, gentle ambient occlusion in corners and under slabs, true isometric 45° camera, seamless neutral backdrop, crisp throughout"  [INSTRUCTION] Render one image of <scene>, deriving every variable from INPUT_TOPIC. prompts.text:
SYSTEM PROMPT: MONUMENTAL HABITAT

You are a landscape photography director and image prompt compiler.

Convert each request into one physically coherent photograph. Build the scene from viewpoint, terrain, scale, weather, light, atmosphere, material, and evidence of life.

Do not assemble a collection of attractive landscape motifs.

Build a place.

1. STRUCTURE

Establish before surface detail:

• camera position and elevation
• camera-to-subject distance
• dominant landform
• foreground, middle distance, background
• horizon placement
• principal visual path
• quiet area
• scale reference

Use one dominant spatial relationship.

Examples:

a small settlement beneath a mountain wall
tiny animals below a dark cliff
two walkers on a narrow ridge
a river leading toward a mountain hidden by cloud
boats crossing open water beneath rock faces
cabins dispersed across overlapping meadow folds

Do not give every region equal importance.

One area dominates.
One supports.
One stays quiet.

2. SCALE

Demonstrate scale through familiar objects:

people, animals, buildings, roads, boats, fences, trees.

Keep them appropriately small when the landscape is the subject.

Human figures are optional.

Do not enlarge people to create a focal point.

Avoid default foreground hikers and staged poses.

Human presence may instead appear through a road, vehicle, smoke, lights, tracks, agriculture, boats, buildings, or infrastructure.

3. TERRAIN

Treat the landscape as continuous geology.

Cliffs support the terrain above them.
Valleys determine drainage.
Rivers occupy low ground.
Waterfalls require upstream water.
Snow follows altitude, exposure, and slope.
Vegetation responds to moisture, elevation, and terrain.
Buildings require foundations and access.

Use erosion, exposed rock, sediment, bare patches, irregular vegetation, weathering, and natural asymmetry.

Do not combine unrelated landforms for spectacle.

4. DEPTH

Create depth through distance and atmospheric visibility.

Foreground:
strongest material separation and local contrast.

Middle distance:
reduced detail and contrast.

Background:
weaker local contrast, atmospheric color shift, partial obscuration where appropriate.

Cloud and fog occupy three-dimensional space.

They may hide ridges, cross valleys, collect against cliffs, or erase part of a summit.

Do not use fog as a decorative overlay.

Do not reveal everything.

5. LIGHT

Use one primary lighting condition.

Examples:

overcast morning
broken-cloud daylight
winter twilight
low side light
post-rain dusk
clear high-altitude daylight
storm-filtered light
blue hour

Light must obey terrain and weather.

A lit slope can exist beside a dark cliff.
Window light remains local.
Wet roads reflect actual sources.
Cloud cover reduces direct illumination.
Shadows may remain dark.

Do not automatically use sunset, rim light, sun rays, glowing clouds, or warm-cool contrast.

6. COLOR

Derive color from materials, weather, and illumination.

Keep neutral colors.

Allow gray skies, dark rock, subdued vegetation, dirty snow, brown earth, weathered timber, and low-saturation distance.

Use strong color only where the environment supports it.

Do not globally increase saturation.

7. MATERIAL

Materials must behave differently.

Rock shows fracture, erosion, moisture, strata, and exposed faces.

Grass forms broad tonal masses before individual blades.

Moss varies in density and reveals underlying stone.

Snow follows terrain and wind exposure.

Water responds to flow, depth, wind, reflection, and disturbance.

Wet roads darken and produce directional reflections.

Buildings show age, construction logic, drainage, foundations, and material variation.

Do not apply equal micro-detail everywhere.

8. ORDINARY EVIDENCE

Retain mundane details when appropriate:

service roads
fences
mud
drainage
utility poles
uneven snow clearance
small sheds
moorings
worn paths
weather stains
different roof ages
animal tracks
patchy vegetation

These elements should remain secondary.

Do not beautify everything.

9. CAMERA

The image must behave as if recorded from one camera position.

Use coherent:

perspective
occlusion
relative scale
focus
atmospheric falloff
exposure
motion

Choose field of view from the required spatial relationship.

Do not use shallow depth of field without a photographic reason.

Avoid stretched wide-angle geometry, excessive local contrast, sharpening halos, artificial HDR, and decorative lens effects.

10. VARIATION

Every new image must materially differ from recent images in at least five areas:

geography
landform
camera elevation
viewing distance
weather
season
lighting
foreground
water structure
human presence
animal presence
settlement
color relationship
visual path

Do not repeatedly generate:

foreground hiker
cliff-edge figure
central waterfall
turquoise river
snowy triangular peaks
sunset
sun rays
wildflower foreground
glowing cabin

If several of these appeared recently, choose another construction.

11. RESTRAINT

Remove elements that do not strengthen the primary relationship.

Five distant horses beneath one dark cliff can be enough.

A cloud-covered mountain and branching river can be enough.

A village beneath snow and low cloud can be enough.

An empty green slope with one band of sunlight can be enough.

Do not add objects merely to fill space.

12. PHYSICAL CHECK

Before generation, silently verify:

Does the terrain connect?

Does water have a source and destination?

Does gravity make sense?

Does the lighting have a source?

Does visibility change correctly with distance?

Do objects agree in scale?

Do feet meet ground?

Do buildings meet terrain?

Do boats sit correctly in water?

Are repeated houses, rocks, trees, and windows naturally varied?

Could one camera have recorded the scene?

Correct failures before output.

13. LANGUAGE

Write with concrete visual instructions.

Avoid:

epic
breathtaking
stunning
masterpiece
award-winning
8K
ultra-detailed
hyperreal
magical
dreamlike
ethereal
otherworldly
cinematic masterpiece
insane detail

Do not substitute adjectives for visual information.

Describe what the camera sees and why it appears that way.

14. MULTIPLE IMAGES

When N images are requested, create N independent photographs.

Each image requires its own:

location type
viewpoint
terrain structure
weather
light
scale reference
foreground
depth structure
color relationship

Never combine them into a grid, collage, contact sheet, diptych, or storyboard.

For 9:16, compose specifically for the vertical frame.

Use the vertical axis for spatial progression rather than cropping a horizontal composition.

FINAL RULE

Geometry before detail.
Light before color grading.
Scale before spectacle.
Atmosphere before effects.
Place before style.

The result should feel observed rather than designed.

MiniMax H3 Prompt
# TACTICAL COMMAND・シネマティック キネティックタイポグラフィ MV 動画プロンプト

※モーショングラフィックステキストを主役にした動画プロンプト。

スタイル:
実写映画＋ハイファッション広告＋タクティカル・ミリタリー＋ディストピアSF＋キネティックタイポグラフィ。
3倍速のハイスピードMV。

ブラック、ダークカーキ、チャコールグレー、アンバーオレンジを基調にした重厚でシネマティックな世界。
巨大な基地、滑走路、作戦司令室、格納庫、装甲車、ヘリコプター、ドローン、レーダー、照準UI、サーチライト、誘導灯、巨大な地形を反復モチーフとして使用する。

画像1の人物と巨大な英語タイポグラフィを同じ3D空間へ配置する。

文字は単なる字幕ではなく、
兵士や車両の隊列、
滑走路のマーキング、
照準UI、
レーダー画面、
ドローンのライト、
格納庫の巨大LED、
誘導灯、
山岳道路の光、
虹彩内部のHUD
として物理的に空間へ存在させる。

文字は、
高速スライド、
急拡大、
隊列による形成、
円形旋回、
レーダースキャン、
奥行き反復、
パース変形、
光点からの形成、
上空からの俯瞰形成、
地面からのせり上がり
など、シーンごとに異なるモーションを使用する。

画像1の人物:
参照画像の顔、髪型、黒い制帽、眼帯、ブラックを基調としたロングコート型衣装、ブーツ、アクセサリー、体格、メイク、配色を全シーンで完全に維持する。
人物の別人化、衣装変更は禁止。

人物は冷静で堂々とした司令官・戦略家のような佇まい。
過剰な戦闘演出よりも、統率・進路・選択・集中をテーマにしたスタイリッシュな映像にする。

重要:
以下の文字を正確なスペルで表示する。

FORGE YOUR PATH
LOCK YOUR FOCUS
RISE ABOVE
SEE THE SIGNAL
MOVE WITH PURPOSE
BUILD YOUR FUTURE
CHOOSE YOUR DIRECTION
STAY THE COURSE
CHOOSE YOUR LIFE

誤字、文字化け、意味不明な文字列、余計な文章を生成しない。
各フレーズは高速モーション中でも最低一度は完全に判読できる状態にする。

カメラ:
クラッシュズーム、
超ローアングル、
超広角、
望遠圧縮、
真上からの俯瞰、
360度オービット、
高速サイドトラッキング、
ドリーズーム、
ドローン視点、
照準器視点、
極端な一点透視、
文字内部への高速突入を多用する。

BGM:
EDM。
参照音源の歌声のみ。
基地の環境音、車両のエンジン音、ヘリコプターのローター音、ドローン、レーダーの電子音、無線ノイズ、足音、誘導灯、巨大扉、低音インパクト、風切り音などの環境音・効果音を入れる。

--------------------------------
シーン1：FORGE YOUR PATH
--------------------------------

広大な荒野に造られた巨大な基地。

画像1の人物が高い指揮台の上から地上を見下ろしている。

眼下には何百人もの隊員、車両、装甲車が巨大な隊列として整然と並んでいる。

真上から見ると、人と車両の配置そのものが、

「FORGE YOUR PATH」

という巨大文字を形成している。

FORGEは最も奥。

YOURは中央。

PATHは人物の真正面から地平線方向へ巨大に伸びる。

最初は隊列がランダムに配置されている。

画像1が片手を上げる。

その瞬間、人と車両が一斉に滑らかに移動。

数秒で巨大なFORGE YOUR PATHへ組み上がる。

カメラは画像1の背後から開始。

人物の肩越しに隊列を映しながら猛烈な速度で上昇。

最後は完全な真上俯瞰へ移行し、巨大な文字全体を見せる。

--------------------------------
シーン2：LOCK YOUR FOCUS
--------------------------------

暗い作戦室。

画像1の人物を横顔からクローズアップ。

人物の正面には大型の精密光学装置と巨大な円形ターゲットUI。

画面中央に、

「LOCK YOUR FOCUS」

が白い巨大文字として表示される。

文字の前後を赤橙色の細い照準ラインが通過する。

最初、FOCUSの文字はわずかにぼやけている。

画像1が光学装置を覗き込む。

円形UIが高速回転。

複数の照準リングが中央へ収束する。

LOCKが上から落ちて固定。

YOURが左右から中央へ接近。

FOCUSが徐々にシャープになり、一瞬完全に静止する。

カメラは人物の瞳→光学レンズ→巨大文字へ高速フォーカス移動。

最後は円形照準UIとLOCK YOUR FOCUSが完全に一直線へ重なる。

--------------------------------
シーン3：RISE ABOVE
--------------------------------

巨大な飛行場。

画像1の人物が両腕を大きく広げ、左右に赤い誘導旗を持って立つ。

上空には何十機ものドローンや航空機が隊列飛行している。

それぞれのライトが空中に点灯し、

「RISE ABOVE」

という巨大な文字を形成する。

RISEが低い位置から上空へ徐々に上昇。

ABOVEはさらに高い空へ巨大化する。

画像1が両腕を上へ振る。

ドローンの隊列も同時に急上昇。

文字全体が空へ持ち上がるように移動する。

カメラは人物の足元から見上げる超ローアングル。

そのまま猛烈な速度で上空へ上昇し、人物を追い越す。

最後は空いっぱいに浮かぶRISE ABOVEを見せる。

--------------------------------
シーン4：SEE THE SIGNAL
--------------------------------

巨大な地下作戦司令室。

壁一面にレーダー、巨大スクリーン、地形図、波形、円形UIが並んでいる。

画像1の人物が巨大な円形コンソールの前に立つ。

中央スクリーンに、

「SEE THE SIGNAL」

が巨大なグリーンホワイト文字として表示される。

最初は大量のノイズ、数字、波形が画面を覆っている。

画像1がコンソールへ手を置く。

円形レーダーが回転。

スキャンラインが画面を一周するたび、不要な情報が消えていく。

最後にSEE THE SIGNALだけが鮮明に残る。

SIGNALの文字から一本の発光ラインが伸び、次の進行方向を示す。

カメラは人物の背後から円形コンソールへ高速接近。

レーダー画面へ突入し、スキャンラインと一緒に360度旋回する。

--------------------------------
シーン5：MOVE WITH PURPOSE
--------------------------------

巨大な航空機格納庫。

画像1の人物が中央に静かに立つ。

左右には車両、隊員、巨大な機械設備が一直線に配置されている。

背後の巨大LEDスクリーンに、

「MOVE WITH PURPOSE」

が白い巨大文字として出現する。

MOVEが左から右へ高速移動。

WITHが人物の背後で静止。

PURPOSEが画面奥から巨大化して前方へ迫る。

画像1が一歩前へ進む。

その一歩を合図に、左右の車両と隊員も同時に整然と前進。

MOVEの文字も人物の歩行速度と完全に同期する。

prompts.text:
SYSTEM PROMPT: MONUMENTAL HABITAT

You are a landscape photography director and image prompt compiler.

Convert each request into one physically coherent photograph. Build the scene from viewpoint, terrain, scale, weather, light, atmosphere, material, and evidence of life.

Do not assemble a collection of attractive landscape motifs.

Build a place.

1. STRUCTURE

Establish before surface detail:

• camera position and elevation
• camera-to-subject distance
• dominant landform
• foreground, middle distance, background
• horizon placement
• principal visual path
• quiet area
• scale reference

Use one dominant spatial relationship.

Examples:

a small settlement beneath a mountain wall
tiny animals below a dark cliff
two walkers on a narrow ridge
a river leading toward a mountain hidden by cloud
boats crossing open water beneath rock faces
cabins dispersed across overlapping meadow folds

Do not give every region equal importance.

One area dominates.
One supports.
One stays quiet.

2. SCALE

Demonstrate scale through familiar objects:

people, animals, buildings, roads, boats, fences, trees.

Keep them appropriately small when the landscape is the subject.

Human figures are optional.

Do not enlarge people to create a focal point.

Avoid default foreground hikers and staged poses.

Human presence may instead appear through a road, vehicle, smoke, lights, tracks, agriculture, boats, buildings, or infrastructure.

3. TERRAIN

Treat the landscape as continuous geology.

Cliffs support the terrain above them.
Valleys determine drainage.
Rivers occupy low ground.
Waterfalls require upstream water.
Snow follows altitude, exposure, and slope.
Vegetation responds to moisture, elevation, and terrain.
Buildings require foundations and access.

Use erosion, exposed rock, sediment, bare patches, irregular vegetation, weathering, and natural asymmetry.

Do not combine unrelated landforms for spectacle.

4. DEPTH

Create depth through distance and atmospheric visibility.

Foreground:
strongest material separation and local contrast.

Middle distance:
reduced detail and contrast.

Background:
weaker local contrast, atmospheric color shift, partial obscuration where appropriate.

Cloud and fog occupy three-dimensional space.

They may hide ridges, cross valleys, collect against cliffs, or erase part of a summit.

Do not use fog as a decorative overlay.

Do not reveal everything.

5. LIGHT

Use one primary lighting condition.

Examples:

overcast morning
broken-cloud daylight
winter twilight
low side light
post-rain dusk
clear high-altitude daylight
storm-filtered light
blue hour

Light must obey terrain and weather.

A lit slope can exist beside a dark cliff.
Window light remains local.
Wet roads reflect actual sources.
Cloud cover reduces direct illumination.
Shadows may remain dark.

Do not automatically use sunset, rim light, sun rays, glowing clouds, or warm-cool contrast.

6. COLOR

Derive color from materials, weather, and illumination.

Keep neutral colors.

Allow gray skies, dark rock, subdued vegetation, dirty snow, brown earth, weathered timber, and low-saturation distance.

Use strong color only where the environment supports it.

Do not globally increase saturation.

7. MATERIAL

Materials must behave differently.

Rock shows fracture, erosion, moisture, strata, and exposed faces.

Grass forms broad tonal masses before individual blades.

Moss varies in density and reveals underlying stone.

Snow follows terrain and wind exposure.

Water responds to flow, depth, wind, reflection, and disturbance.

Wet roads darken and produce directional reflections.

Buildings show age, construction logic, drainage, foundations, and material variation.

Do not apply equal micro-detail everywhere.

8. ORDINARY EVIDENCE

Retain mundane details when appropriate:

service roads
fences
mud
drainage
utility poles
uneven snow clearance
small sheds
moorings
worn paths
weather stains
different roof ages
animal tracks
patchy vegetation

These elements should remain secondary.

Do not beautify everything.

9. CAMERA

The image must behave as if recorded from one camera position.

Use coherent:

perspective
occlusion
relative scale
focus
atmospheric falloff
exposure
motion

Choose field of view from the required spatial relationship.

Do not use shallow depth of field without a photographic reason.

Avoid stretched wide-angle geometry, excessive local contrast, sharpening halos, artificial HDR, and decorative lens effects.

10. VARIATION

Every new image must materially differ from recent images in at least five areas:

geography
landform
camera elevation
viewing distance
weather
season
lighting
foreground
water structure
human presence
animal presence
settlement
color relationship
visual path

Do not repeatedly generate:

foreground hiker
cliff-edge figure
central waterfall
turquoise river
snowy triangular peaks
sunset
sun rays
wildflower foreground
glowing cabin

If several of these appeared recently, choose another construction.

11. RESTRAINT

Remove elements that do not strengthen the primary relationship.

Five distant horses beneath one dark cliff can be enough.

A cloud-covered mountain and branching river can be enough.

A village beneath snow and low cloud can be enough.

An empty green slope with one band of sunlight can be enough.

Do not add objects merely to fill space.

12. PHYSICAL CHECK

Before generation, silently verify:

Does the terrain connect?

Does water have a source and destination?

Does gravity make sense?

Does the lighting have a source?

Does visibility change correctly with distance?

Do objects agree in scale?

Do feet meet ground?

Do buildings meet terrain?

Do boats sit correctly in water?

Are repeated houses, rocks, trees, and windows naturally varied?

Could one camera have recorded the scene?

Correct failures before output.

13. LANGUAGE

Write with concrete visual instructions.

Avoid:

epic
breathtaking
stunning
masterpiece
award-winning
8K
ultra-detailed
hyperreal
magical
dreamlike
ethereal
otherworldly
cinematic masterpiece
insane detail

Do not substitute adjectives for visual information.

Describe what the camera sees and why it appears that way.

14. MULTIPLE IMAGES

When N images are requested, create N independent photographs.

Each image requires its own:

location type
viewpoint
terrain structure
weather
light
scale reference
foreground
depth structure
color relationship

Never combine them into a grid, collage, contact sheet, diptych, or storyboard.

For 9:16, compose specifically for the vertical frame.

Use the vertical axis for spatial progression rather than cropping a horizontal composition.

FINAL RULE

Geometry before detail.
Light before color grading.
Scale before spectacle.
Atmosphere before effects.
Place before style.

The result should feel observed rather than designed.

Vertical streetwear campaign poster: a woman with the face from the reference photo stands frontally at the center of an arid dusk plain, arms hanging at her sides, shoulders relaxed, looking straight into the lens with a completely neutral catalogue expression, no gesture. Around her, articulated zebra skeletons stand scattered across the plain in near-perfect symmetry — two large ones cropped by the left and right frame edges, two mid-sized further in, one small at center right — the fan arrangement building depth through decreasing scale. Lighting, deliberately inconsistent between layers: the subject lit with soft even frontal studio light, broad fill, no hard shadows, flat descriptive modelling on the face; the environment lit by a low side source throwing long skeleton shadows to the right, plus a blue backlight at the horizon igniting the mist. She casts her own shorter, softer shadow to the right to bed her in. Camera: vertical framing at chest height, frontal and centered, medium-long focal length with no distortion, deep depth of field with atmospheric rather than optical falloff. Typographic layer: three lines of scattered alphanumeric characters interspersed with pedestrian pictograms across the top, in wide-tracked white condensed sans-serif — signage or inventory-code language; at the bottom center, a brand name in a narrow serif with a small sans-serif line beneath it. One stays quiet.

2. SCALE

Demonstrate scale through familiar objects:

people, animals, buildings, roads, boats, fences, trees.

Keep them appropriately small when the landscape is the subject.

Human figures are optional.

Do not enlarge people to create a focal point.

Avoid default foreground hikers and staged poses.

Human presence may instead appear through a road, vehicle, smoke, lights, tracks, agriculture, boats, buildings, or infrastructure.

3. TERRAIN

Treat the landscape as continuous geology.

Cliffs support the terrain above them.
Valleys determine drainage.
Rivers occupy low ground.
Waterfalls require upstream water.
Snow follows altitude, exposure, and slope.
Vegetation responds to moisture, elevation, and terrain.
Buildings require foundations and access.

Use erosion, exposed rock, sediment, bare patches, irregular vegetation, weathering, and natural asymmetry.

Do not combine unrelated landforms for spectacle.

4. DEPTH

Create depth through distance and atmospheric visibility.

Foreground:
strongest material separation and local contrast.

Middle distance:
reduced detail and contrast.

Background:
weaker local contrast, atmospheric color shift, partial obscuration where appropriate.

Cloud and fog occupy three-dimensional space.

They may hide ridges, cross valleys, collect against cliffs, or erase part of a summit.

Do not use fog as a decorative overlay.

Do not reveal everything.

5. LIGHT

Use one primary lighting condition.

Examples:

overcast morning
broken-cloud daylight
winter twilight
low side light
post-rain dusk
clear high-altitude daylight
storm-filtered light
blue hour

Light must obey terrain and weather.

A lit slope can exist beside a dark cliff.
Window light remains local.
Wet roads reflect actual sources.
Cloud cover reduces direct illumination.
Shadows may remain dark.

Do not automatically use sunset, rim light, sun rays, glowing clouds, or warm-cool contrast.

6. COLOR

Derive color from materials, weather, and illumination.

Keep neutral colors.

Allow gray skies, dark rock, subdued vegetation, dirty snow, brown earth, weathered timber, and low-saturation distance.

Use strong color only where the environment supports it.

Do not globally increase saturation.

7. MATERIAL

Materials must behave differently.

Rock shows fracture, erosion, moisture, strata, and exposed faces.

Grass forms broad tonal masses before individual blades.

Moss varies in density and reveals underlying stone.

Snow follows terrain and wind exposure.

Water responds to flow, depth, wind, reflection, and disturbance.

Wet roads darken and produce directional reflections.

Buildings show age, construction logic, drainage, foundations, and material variation.

Do not apply equal micro-detail everywhere.

8. ORDINARY EVIDENCE

Retain mundane details when appropriate:

service roads
fences
mud
drainage
utility poles
uneven snow clearance
small sheds
moorings
worn paths
weather stains
different roof ages
animal tracks
patchy vegetation

These elements should remain secondary.

Do not beautify everything.

9. CAMERA

The image must behave as if recorded from one camera position.

Use coherent:

perspective
occlusion
relative scale
focus
atmospheric falloff
exposure
motion

Choose field of view from the required spatial relationship.

Do not use shallow depth of field without a photographic reason.

Avoid stretched wide-angle geometry, excessive local contrast, sharpening halos, artificial HDR, and decorative lens effects.

10. VARIATION

Every new image must materially differ from recent images in at least five areas:

geography
landform
camera elevation
viewing distance
weather
season
lighting
foreground
water structure
human presence
animal presence
settlement
color relationship
visual path

Do not repeatedly generate:

foreground hiker
cliff-edge figure
central waterfall
turquoise river
snowy triangular peaks
sunset
sun rays
wildflower foreground
glowing cabin

If several of these appeared recently, choose another construction.

11. RESTRAINT

Remove elements that do not strengthen the primary relationship.

Five distant horses beneath one dark cliff can be enough.

A cloud-covered mountain and branching river can be enough.

A village beneath snow and low cloud can be enough.

An empty green slope with one band of sunlight can be enough.

Do not add objects merely to fill space.

12. PHYSICAL CHECK

Before generation, silently verify:

Does the terrain connect?

Does water have a source and destination?

Does gravity make sense?

Does the lighting have a source?

Does visibility change correctly with distance?

Do objects agree in scale?

Do feet meet ground?

Do buildings meet terrain?

Do boats sit correctly in water?

Are repeated houses, rocks, trees, and windows naturally varied?

Could one camera have recorded the scene?

Correct failures before output.

13. LANGUAGE

Write with concrete visual instructions.

Avoid:

epic
breathtaking
stunning
masterpiece
award-winning
8K
ultra-detailed
hyperreal
magical
dreamlike
ethereal
otherworldly
cinematic masterpiece
insane detail

Do not substitute adjectives for visual information.

Describe what the camera sees and why it appears that way.

14. MULTIPLE IMAGES

When N images are requested, create N independent photographs.

Each image requires its own:

location type
viewpoint
terrain structure
weather
light
scale reference
foreground
depth structure
color relationship

Never combine them into a grid, collage, contact sheet, diptych, or storyboard.

For 9:16, compose specifically for the vertical frame.

Use the vertical axis for spatial progression rather than cropping a horizontal composition.

FINAL RULE

Geometry before detail.
Light before color grading.
Scale before spectacle.
Atmosphere before effects.
Place before style.

The result should feel observed rather than designed.

Prompts I used for Seedance 2.0

Create a 15-second, 1080p ultra-realistic documentary-style personal smartphone video showing a young Korean woman walking through Seoul on her way to surprise her boyfriend at work. The footage should feel spontaneous, intimate, imperfect, genuinely self-recorded, and emotionally natural rather than performed. MAIN SUBJECT The same young Korean woman in her early 20s throughout this video and all continuation videos. Naturally attractive with realistic skin texture, minimal makeup, expressive dark eyes, naturally styled medium-length dark hair, and a warm youthful appearance. She wears a simple light grey oversized cardigan over a white top, relaxed dark trousers, comfortable sneakers, a small shoulder bag, and understated jewelry. Keep her face, identity, body proportions, hairstyle, clothing, accessories, phone, bag, and overall appearance completely consistent throughout this video and all following videos. She is carrying a small paper gift bag containing a surprise for her boyfriend. LOCATION A lively but ordinary Seoul neighborhood during early evening, transitioning gradually toward a restaurant district. Narrow sidewalks, residential buildings mixed with small businesses, convenience stores, parked bicycles, scooters, utility poles, street trees, crosswalks, warm restaurant windows beginning to illuminate, pedestrians naturally passing in the distance, and normal evening traffic. The environment should feel authentically lived-in rather than designed as a tourist location. CAMERA / VISUAL STYLE Authentic casual smartphone footage filmed entirely by the woman herself. Most footage is front-facing selfie video while she walks, occasionally switching to the rear camera to show where she is going. Natural arm movement creates subtle smartphone shake. Her face occasionally moves partially outside the frame because she is watching the sidewalk instead of carefully composing herself. Include imperfect autofocus, automatic exposure changes, slight rolling shutter during quick turns, natural smartphone sharpening, mild compression, realistic microphone handling noise, occasional wind interference, and imperfect framing. No stabilization, gimbal movement, drone shots, cinematic camera choreography, dramatic lighting, slow motion, professional depth of field, commercial color grading, or polished cinematography. The footage should genuinely feel like a woman casually recording something for herself while preparing to surprise someone she loves. 00:00-00:05 — ON MY WAY Begin immediately with front-facing smartphone footage as she walks quickly along a Seoul sidewalk, holding the phone slightly below eye level while the image gently bounces with every step. She is visibly excited and struggles slightly to hide her smile. She briefly raises the small paper gift bag into frame and looks directly into the phone. She speaks casually in Korean while walking: “지금 남자친구 일하는 데 가고 있어요. 제가 오는 거 전혀 몰라요.” She gives a small excited laugh after speaking, lowers the gift bag, checks the road ahead, then looks back into the phone. Do not make her delivery sound rehearsed or influencer-like. She is recording a private personal moment. 00:05-00:10 — ALMOST THERE She switches to the rear smartphone camera while continuing to walk, revealing the street ahead with glowing restaurant windows, pedestrians, parked scooters, and evening traffic. Her hand holding the gift bag occasionally enters the bottom of the frame. She quietly says from behind the camera: “진짜 놀라겠지?” The camera briefly points toward the ground as she steps around another pedestrian, then naturally rises again. She crosses a small street and approaches the restaurant where her boyfriend works. 00:10-00:15 — HIS RESTAURANT Still using the rear camera, she approaches a warm, intimate restaurant with large front windows. Through the glass, several occupied tables are visible, but she does not immediately search carefully for her boyfriend. She quietly laughs and says: “여기다.” She switches back to the front-facing camera for a moment, gives the camera an excited nervous smile, raises the gift bag beside her face, then turns the phone toward the restaurant entrance as she reaches for the door. Cut abruptly while her hand begins opening it. No fade. PHYSICAL REALISM Maintain believable smartphone movement and natural walking physics. Her hand, fingers, phone, gift bag, clothing, hair, shoulder bag, reflections, pedestrians, vehicles, doors, and background objects must behave naturally. The gift bag remains physically consistent and stays with her throughout the sequence. AUDIO Natural environmental audio only. Footsteps, passing traffic, distant conversations, occasional bicycle sounds, fabric movement, paper bag movement, pedestrian ambience, restaurant noise becoming gradually audible, smartphone microphone handling, and her Korean dialogue. No music. No narration. No soundtrack. No subtitles. FINAL FEEL The emotional tone should be innocent, warm, excited, intimate, and completely ordinary. Nothing should suggest betrayal yet. The audience should experience her anticipation without knowing what she is about to discover. It should feel like a genuine forgotten smartphone recording rather than a scripted drama.

Use the provided reference images with strict identity and environment continuity throughout the entire video.

@Image1, Girlfriend Reference: Use Image 1 as the exact visual reference for the girlfriend. Preserve her face, facial proportions, skin tone, hairstyle, hair length, body proportions, clothing, shoulder bag, gift bag, accessories, and overall appearance. She is physically holding the smartphone throughout the recording and therefore must never appear from an impossible external camera angle.

@Image2, Boyfriend Reference: Use Image 2 as the exact visual reference for the boyfriend. Preserve his face, naturally messy dark hair, skin texture, body proportions, clothing, and overall appearance throughout every moment in which he is visible.

@Image3, Other Woman Reference: Use Image 3 as the exact visual reference for the young woman having dinner with the boyfriend. Preserve her face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions, and overall appearance consistently. She should appear naturally dressed for an ordinary intimate dinner rather than exaggeratedly glamorous.

@Image4, Restaurant Reference: Use Image 4 as the exact environmental reference for the restaurant, preserving its architecture, table arrangement, wooden furniture, pendant lighting, wall materials, windows, decorative elements, color temperature, spatial layout, and overall evening atmosphere.

Do not blend facial characteristics between @Image1, @Image2, or @Image3. Each person must remain visually distinct and consistently match their corresponding reference.

Continuity: Continue directly from the previous personal recording. The same young Korean woman from @Image1 has arrived at the restaurant where she believes her boyfriend from @Image2 is working. She intends to surprise him and secretly capture his reaction on her phone, completely unaware that he is actually sitting inside having an intimate dinner with the woman from @Image3.

Environment: Use @Image4 as the restaurant environment throughout the sequence. It is a small intimate Seoul restaurant during evening service, filled with warm pendant lighting, wooden tables, softly illuminated windows, simple contemporary decor, plates, glasses, subtle candlelight, quiet customers, and staff naturally moving through the background. Preserve the restaurant's spatial geography from beginning to end.

The boyfriend from @Image2 and the other woman from @Image3 are seated together at a small table farther inside the restaurant. Their table contains two meals, two drinks, ordinary tableware, and a small candle. The romantic context should come primarily from their relaxed body language, prolonged attention toward each other, smiles, and subtle physical contact rather than exaggerated decorations.

Camera / Visual Style: The entire video is captured through the rear-facing smartphone camera physically held by @Image1. Never introduce an external camera operator. The girlfriend herself remains behind the phone throughout the recording.

Use authentic personal smartphone footage with natural walking bounce, imperfect framing, subtle hand tremors, occasional focus hunting, automatic exposure correction, realistic shadow noise, slight digital compression, imperfect white balance, minor rolling shutter during faster movements, microphone handling noise, and unplanned camera adjustments.

The camera must never anticipate the discovery. During the first section, it casually searches the restaurant because she genuinely expects to find her boyfriend working. Only after she recognizes him should the camera behavior change from excited exploration into almost motionless disbelief and then unstable shock.

Emotional Progression: Excited anticipation → casual searching → confusion → recognition → disbelief → silent heartbreak → mutual recognition.

Dialogue Rule: All spoken dialogue must be natural Korean. No English dialogue, no subtitles, no narration, and no translated voice-over.

Audio Design: Natural restaurant audio only, including quiet Korean conversations, glasses touching tables, plates, cutlery, chairs moving, footsteps, distant kitchen activity, door movement, fabric sounds, gift-bag paper rustling, smartphone handling noise, and the girlfriend's changing breathing. No background music and no artificial dramatic sound effects.

[3] TIMESTAMPED STORYBOARD

[00:00-00:05] ENTERING WITH THE SURPRISE

Continue directly from the previous recording with @Image1 quietly pushing open the restaurant entrance while recording through her phone's rear-facing camera. The exterior evening light briefly causes the smartphone exposure to struggle as she enters the darker warm interior from @Image4, creating a natural moment of overexposure followed by automatic correction as the restaurant's pendant lights, tables, customers, and wooden surfaces gradually become properly exposed.

She walks slowly between tables while trying not to attract attention because she wants to secretly record her boyfriend's reaction when he notices her. The gift bag remains physically held low beside her body and occasionally enters the bottom edge of the frame as her arm moves naturally.

The phone casually scans staff members and tables while she searches for @Image2. She quietly whispers from behind the camera in Korean:

“어디 있지...”

She continues walking.

Nothing in her movement, breathing, or camera behavior should suggest that she knows what she is about to discover.

[00:05-00:10] THAT'S HIM

As @Image1 moves around a partial divider inside @Image4, the rear smartphone camera casually pans across several occupied tables.

@Image2 becomes visible approximately several tables away.

The camera initially passes across him because she expects to see him working and does not immediately understand why he is sitting down.

She abruptly stops walking.

The camera movement stops half a second later, reflecting the delayed reaction of her hand.

She slowly moves the phone back toward the same table.

Now establish clearly that @Image2 is seated opposite @Image3.

He is not wearing restaurant work attire and is completely relaxed, smiling warmly while speaking quietly with her over dinner.

The smartphone autofocus initially locks onto a foreground chair, briefly making the couple soft and indistinct before naturally correcting and focusing on @Image2 and @Image3.

@Image3 smiles at something he says and gently reaches across the table, placing her fingers over his hand.

@Image2 does not pull away.

Instead, his hand subtly turns beneath hers and they remain touching.

Keep the gesture extremely natural and understated.

The phone becomes almost completely motionless.

The girlfriend says nothing.

Her previously relaxed breathing quietly stops for a moment.

[00:10-00:13] REALIZATION

Maintain the imperfect distant smartphone composition without cutting to a cinematic close-up. @Image2 and @Image3 remain at exactly the same table positions with consistent food, glasses, candle, clothing, and lighting.

@Image2 leans slightly closer toward @Image3 while speaking softly. Their conversation should remain largely unintelligible from the girlfriend's position because restaurant ambience separates them.

The girlfriend's arm unconsciously drops.

As a result, the smartphone framing tilts slightly downward and the top of her gift bag slowly enters the bottom of the frame.

Its paper handles tremble subtly.

Her breathing becomes audible again, but now it is slower, heavier, and unsteady.

She whispers almost involuntarily:

“뭐야...?”

Do not immediately make her cry.

Her dominant reaction is disbelief.

[00:13-00:15] HE SEES HER

At approximately 00:13, @Image2 casually turns his head while still seated and looks across the restaurant.

His eyes find the girlfriend.

His expression changes immediately.

The relaxed smile disappears.

His body becomes completely still.

His hand remains near @Image3's hand for a fraction of a second before instinctively pulling away.

@Image3 notices his sudden reaction and looks toward him in confusion before beginning to follow his gaze toward the girlfriend.

The smartphone camera shakes sharply for the first time because @Image1 realizes that he has seen her.

The gift bag swings slightly into frame.

@Image2 begins pushing his chair backward as though preparing to stand.

Do not allow him to reach her.

Do not begin a confrontation.

Do not show the girlfriend from another perspective.

At exactly 00:15, abruptly terminate the smartphone recording while the camera is still shaking.

Hard cut to black. No fade.

[4] GLOBAL SUPPLEMENT

The sequence must feel like an authentic continuation of a private smartphone recording rather than a professionally produced cheating scene. The emotional impact should come from the fact that @Image1 entered the restaurant expecting to preserve a happy surprise and accidentally recorded the exact moment she discovered the betrayal.

Maintain absolute reference consistency:

@Image1 = girlfriend only

@Image2 = boyfriend only

@Image3 = other woman only

@Image4 = restaurant environment only

Never merge identities, swap faces, change hairstyles, alter clothing, replace characters, or reinterpret one reference as another character.

The smartphone remains physically controlled by @Image1 throughout the entire 15 seconds. Every visible camera movement must therefore correspond naturally to her walking, stopping, breathing, lowering her arm, trembling, or reacting. Never show her full body or face from an external viewpoint unless naturally visible through an existing mirror or reflection, and avoid even those reflections unless necessary.

Preserve continuous restaurant geography. The entrance, divider, boyfriend's table, neighboring customers, walls, windows, pendant lights, and surrounding furniture must remain spatially consistent as she walks deeper into the restaurant.

The boyfriend must not notice her prematurely. From 00:00 through approximately 00:13, he remains completely unaware that she has entered. His attention remains naturally focused on @Image3. Only near the end should he casually look across the room, recognize @Image1, freeze, and begin reacting.

The romantic relationship between @Image2 and @Image3 should be communicated through believable subtle behavior rather than exaggerated cheating imagery. Their quiet smiles, close attention, intimate conversation, relaxed posture, shared dinner, candle, prolonged eye contact, and gentle hand contact are sufficient.

The girlfriend's emotional change must remain restrained and physically believable. Do not use screaming, dramatic crying, confrontation, dropping the phone, throwing the gift, dramatic zooming, running, or theatrical reactions. Her shock appears through silence, interrupted breathing, a lowered arm, trembling paper handles, unstable framing, and the eventual sharp camera shake when their eyes meet.

No cinematic inserts. No external reaction shot. No shot-reverse-shot. No third-person camera. No dolly movement. No slow motion. No dramatic zoom. No artificial rack focus. No soundtrack. No subtitles. No narration. No dramatic sound design.

The final result should feel uncomfortably real, accidental, intimate, imperfect, spontaneous, emotionally restrained, and deeply personal, as though the viewer is watching the exact private recording captured on her phone when a planned romantic surprise unexpectedly became the moment she discovered her boyfriend with someone else.

Prompt:

Vertical studio fashion editorial with an absurdist set-up: a woman with the face from the reference photo sits sunk deep into a black leather recliner in a fog-lit studio, one leg stretched straight toward the camera and the other bent, counting a thick stack of banknotes with both hands at chest height, eyes down on the money, expression completely neutral — no smile, no gesture, that indifference being what makes the joke work. Around her, a ring of live brown hens walks across the studio floor, several cropped by the left and right frame edges so more are implied off-camera, and loose banknotes are scattered across the floor. Wardrobe (womenswear): a cropped boxy black-and-white colour-blocked faux-leather jacket with a spread shirt collar, black sleeves, yellow and side panels and white curved front panels, worn open with the zipper down; an oversized plain white t-shirt underneath showing at the hem; a fine silver chain necklace with a small cross pendant; extremely wide-leg washed charcoal-grey denim cargo trousers with large flap side pockets and a cream drawstring hanging at the waist; and white leather Air Force-style low-top sneakers; dark curly hair. Camera — the main device: a very wide lens, 16–20mm, with the body almost resting on the floor. The extended foot closest to the lens is grossly enlarged and distorted, filling the entire lower third of the frame, while the body compresses backward and the head sits relatively small at the top; that proximity-scale exaggeration is what creates the sense of dominance — the viewer is literally at her feet. A strong diagonal runs from the foreground sneaker up to the face. Lighting: a single large soft key from above and slightly in front — short shadows under the chin and beneath the recliner, gentle modelling on the arm, specular sheen along the faux-leather panels, and clear falloff toward the corners and the back of the set; no strong side fill, so the flanks of the chair and the outermost hens drop to dark values; a faint second source behind right putting a rim on her shoulder and on the feathers of the hens on that side. Atmosphere: fine haze in the air separating the subject from the background and letting the grey cyclorama gradient from mid grey down to near black in the upper corners — real light falloff through smoke, not a digital vignette. Focus: relatively deep depth of field despite the angle — both the foreground sneaker and the face legible, with slight softening on the hens at the back, consistent with a wide lens stopped down. Grade: cool and desaturated environment with a blue-green cast in the cyclorama shadows, the only warmth coming from the hens’ red-brown feathers and the skin tones; medium-high contrast, dense blacks, controlled highlights, fine grain. Palette: cool cyclorama greys filling the background echoed by the washed charcoal denim, black leather and black recliner as the central anchoring mass, the white jacket panels and white tee as the single bright block placed exactly at the center of the body, warm brown feathers distributed in a ring around it, and the muted green of the banknotes plus the white sneakers as scattered light values across the lower third.

Create a 3:4 vertical, realistic indoor digital portrait of a clearly adult woman in her early-to-late twenties, standing against a completely plain warm gray-white wall. Frame her from the head down to roughly the thighs or knees, with generous negative space above her head. She has a deep brown, almost black, chin-length bob with softly inward-curving ends and thin blunt bangs separated into small natural strands. The hair should be smooth but not synthetic, retaining a little natural flyaway texture and subtle warm-brown reflections in the light.

She looks directly into the camera while placing both hands behind her head or at the back of her hair, opening her elbows widely to form a broad triangular frame around her face and shoulders. Do not make the elbows perfectly level or the shoulders mechanically symmetrical. Let most of her weight rest on one leg while the other leg shifts slightly forward or sideways, producing a small natural hip shift and an understated S-curve through the torso. The pose should feel like a spontaneous social-media portrait pose that she happened to hold for a moment, not a precisely choreographed fashion pose.

Dress her in a black velvet modernized qipao-inspired mini dress: sleeveless, halter-style, with a high or mandarin-collar impression, several black Chinese-style frog closures running down the center chest, and small vertical openings between the closures. The fitted skirt ends around the upper-to-mid thigh and features a high side slit revealing part of one upper thigh. The velvet should absorb most light and remain deep black, showing only soft silver-black reflections along folds, curved areas and the hem. Never make the material look like latex, PVC or glossy leather. Add delicate black lace ruffled wrist cuffs on both wrists.

Visible skin includes the face, most of the neck, both shoulders, upper arms, underarm areas, part of the forearms, and both thighs beneath the hem and through the side slit. The chest and waist remain mostly covered. Skin is light neutral-to-slightly-warm, brightened by the contrast with the black dress without becoming pure white. It should look fine-textured and soft, as though it would feel warm, smooth and gently resistant to the touch rather than ceramic or plastic. Preserve faint pores, tiny tonal changes around the elbows and underarms, and subtle real-skin irregularities.

Keep a compact oval face, delicate short chin, large-eye visual balance, refined nose bridge and slender facial proportions. Makeup follows a soft K-pop idol glam blended with Japanese doll-like portrait makeup: light semi-matte foundation, thin elongated black eyeliner, individually separated lashes, very subtle aegyo-sal with muted pink-brown lower-eye shading, a cool gray-blue contact-lens-like iris appearance, naturally slim brows, restrained nose contour, and muted rose-bean or soft brown-red lips. Her eyes remain fully open and fixed on the lens. Her lips are closed or barely parted with only the slightest upward curve, creating a composed expression that feels as though she has already held the pose for several seconds.

Photograph it like a premium smartphone or compact digital camera portrait taken casually in a room, not a commercial studio campaign. Use perspective comparable to a 35–50mm full-frame equivalent lens, with the camera around chest-to-shoulder height, nearly frontal and just slightly below eye level. Allow a tiny framing offset or subtle tilt instead of mathematically perfect centering. Rendering should be slightly soft, with mild consumer-camera texture, faint sensor grain, low-to-moderate contrast and natural edge softness rather than aggressive sharpening.

The primary physical light source is a large window positioned front-right of the camera, producing broad diffused daylight. It first illuminates the right cheek, shoulder, upper arm and legs with wide creamy highlights that remain low in oiliness. The left side receives only gentle wall-bounce fill and gradually falls darker. No hard flash, no dramatic rim light and no sharp studio shadows. The wall itself should be a little brighter on the right and subtly darker on the left, with minor unevenness that feels like genuine room light.

The final atmosphere is quiet, soft-dark, slightly doll-like and subtly intimate, combining a black modernized qipao, short bob hairstyle and minimalist East Asian social-media portrait aesthetic. It feels as if she had already tried several poses beside the window that afternoon; a second earlier she was adjusting her hair, the camera caught the brief pause with both hands behind her head, and a second later she might lower her arms again. Preserve the slightly uneven shoulder line, imperfect elbow positions, natural skin-tone variation and faint digital noise so the image feels photographed by a real person rather than polished into an immaculate AI advertisement.

Negative prompt: underage, childlike body, extra fingers, deformed hands, warped arms, broken elbows, plastic skin, porcelain skin, extreme hourglass, oversized breasts, latex dress, PVC shine, busy background, neon lighting, hard flash, strong rim light, mirror selfie, phone in hand, over-retouched, over-sharpened, heavy bokeh.
